Select differential edges with Bayesian FDR control

Source: R/diff.R
select_diff_edges.Rd

Computes a per-edge posterior probability that two groups differ and selects edges with bayes_fdr(). Chains are pooled by default.

Usage

select_diff_edges(
  fit,
  groups = c(1, 2),
  alpha = 0.05,
  rule = c("magnitude", "structural", "union", "cut"),
  delta = 0.05,
  scale = c("pcor", "precision"),
  chain = NULL,
  decision = c("bfdr", "median"),
  c = delta
)

Arguments

fit

A multiggm_fit or multiggm_fit_list object.

groups

Integer vector of length 2, the groups c(k, m) to compare. Default c(1, 2).

alpha

Target posterior expected FDR. Default 0.05.

rule
"magnitude"

(default) \(P(|D_{ij}| > c)\), where \(D\) is the group difference on scale. Works for every sampler. FDR is controlled for the hypothesis \(|D_{ij}| > c\): a true difference smaller than c counts as a null.

"structural"

\(P(G_{s,ij} \ne G_{t,ij})\), the posterior probability that the edge is in exactly one of the two graphs. For mGHS, \(P(S_s \ne S_t)\) with \(S = 1(w > 0.5)\) on the shrinkage weight. Detects edges present in one group only, not changes in strength.

"union"

\(P(\textrm{structural difference or } |D_{ij}| > c)\), counted per iteration (mGHS: the cut-model indicator is the structural part). Detects both deletions and changes in strength.

"cut"

mGHS only: \(P(Z_s \ne Z_t)\) for the cut-model indicator.

See edge_probs() for the exact definitions.

delta, c

Threshold \(c\) for the magnitude and union rules, on the scale given by scale: the smallest difference worth detecting. c is an alias of delta (default 0.05). c may also be the result of calibrate_c(), whose suggested_c is then used (pcor scale only). A fixed c that is not well above the sampling noise of \(D\) gives many false calls; see calibrate_c().

scale

"pcor" (default) for partial correlations or "precision" for precision-matrix entries.

chain

NULL (default) pools all chains; an integer vector selects chains of a multiggm_fit_list.

decision

"bfdr" (default) selects the largest set with posterior expected FDR at most alpha (bayes_fdr(), keeping tied probabilities together); "median" selects probability > 0.5.

Value

An object of class "multiggm_diff_selection": a list with selected (symmetric logical [p, p] matrix), prob (symmetric [p, p] matrix of the edge probabilities used), edges (data frame of the selected edges with i, j, prob, q_value (see bfdr_qvalues()) and, for the magnitude rule, mean difference), expected_fdr (posterior expected FDR of the selected set), n_selected, alpha, rule, delta (the threshold used, or NA), scale, groups and decision.

See also

diff_summary(), bayes_fdr(), pip_diff_edge()

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiggm(K = 2, p = 8, n = 80, seed = 1)
fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, burnin = 200, nsave = 100)
sel <- select_diff_edges(fit, alpha = 0.1, delta = 0.1)
sel
#> <multiggm_diff_selection>
#>   Groups 1 vs 2, rule: magnitude (c = 0.1, pcor scale), decision: bfdr
#>   Selected 6 edges at target FDR 0.1 (posterior expected FDR 0.033)
#>   i j prob    q_value       mean
#> 1 1 2 1.00 0.00000000 -0.5458386
#> 2 2 4 1.00 0.00000000  0.4192926
#> 3 2 5 1.00 0.00000000  0.4815726
#> 4 3 4 0.98 0.00500000  0.4992961
#> 5 7 8 0.93 0.01800000  0.3279500
#> 6 4 6 0.89 0.03333333 -0.2481891
